A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same representation-disentanglement work, renamed from SEER to TELLME. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original disentanglement, safety-classification, and detoxification experiments, including loss ablations and additional model evaluations in its appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds target-layer experiments, CoLA and SiQA evaluations, and a monitoring case study.

M1.justification: SEER becomes TELLME, but Equations 1–5 and Algorithm 1 retain the same contrastive-pair construction, InfoNCE objective, representation and output retention terms, and optimization procedure. LoRA editing, the NT-Xent alternative, and applications before or after SFT already appear in v1.

E1.justification: v2 Appendix B.8 adds training and evaluation on grammatical acceptability through CoLA and social commonsense through SiQA. These extend direct task applications beyond v1's safety classification and detoxification, while retaining the mathematics, knowledge, and safety evaluations. Renaming safety classification as monitoring does not itself change coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding safety comparison retains Self-Sim, Linear Probe, Latent Guard, and SFT. Detoxification comparisons and the five contrastive-loss alternatives are also retained. The new general-task tables compare the original and edited model without introducing another comparison method.

E3.justification: v2 introduces target-layer sweeps on Llama-3.1-8B and protocols for the added CoLA and SiQA experiments. Its main monitoring table omits Gemma2-9B, reducing that comparison from four backbones to three. Existing split and hyperparameter descriptions remain stable. The monitoring plot includes 10–90% depth, although Appendix B.7 describes 20–90%.

E4.justification: New Appendix B.7 tests target-layer sensitivity for general capability, monitoring accuracy, and detoxification. Appendix D.1 adds a privacy-risk misclassification case with before-and-after representation similarities. These supplement the retained contrastive-loss and retention-loss ablations; moving the latter into main-text Table 4 is not a new analysis.

E5.justification: v2 Table 11 newly reports a standard deviation of 0.47% for MMLU accuracy across target-layer choices. This measures dispersion across configurations, not uncertainty across repeated training runs. Neither version reports experimental seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: v1 Table 3 becomes v2 Table 5 with revised Self-Sim and Linear Probe scores and removed Gemma2-9B rows. Qwen2.5-7B multi-risk Linear Probe original/edited scores change from 93.1/91.9 to 69.4/77.4, reversing the reported effect. New Tables 12–13 report original/edited performance of 69.13/75.84 on CoLA and 79.92/80.2 on SiQA; layer results and a monitoring case are also added. Existing disentanglement and detoxification scores are retained.

T1.justification: v2 Section 2.2 explicitly expands the classifier formulation to include a direct representation-based monitor, g = ψ, alongside the output-based composition described in v1 Section 3.2. The Wasserstein and k-variance definitions, generalization bound, and appendix proof and assumptions otherwise remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The headline contribution changes from providing faithful self-explanations of inference logic to enhancing transparency so monitors can identify sensitive behaviors more reliably. The introduction and conclusion additionally position the approach as potentially enabling scalable oversight of superintelligence. This substantially changes the central claim and intended significance beyond the method rename.

C2.justification: New Appendix E limits effectiveness by pretrained knowledge and behaviors represented during training, noting that unseen or irrelevant behaviors may remain unchanged and that only post-training was studied. v2 also interprets the layer analyses and proposes that monitorability may improve with model capability. Existing generalization and retention-loss interpretations largely remain.

D1.justification: v1 describes the retain dataset generically; v2 identifies it as UltraChat. Appendix B.3 adds complete binary- and multi-risk SFT prompts, supervision details, and an explicit 16,000-example training description. Appendix B.2 newly reports approximately eight hours on four GPUs. These are added disclosures rather than demonstrated changes to existing experiments.

R1.justification: Research positioning shifts from self-explanation and interpretability toward AI control and monitoring. New citations and discussion cover alignment faking, reasoning-model explanation unfaithfulness, transparency, and causal rationalization. Several earlier interpretability references, including Interpretability Needs a New Paradigm, are removed. This exceeds a citation-format or bibliography update.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around monitoring, with widespread changes from concepts and self-explainability to behaviors and transparency. Related work and Algorithm 1 move into appendices, while retention-loss ablation material enters the main text. The author list also adds Lijie Hu.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, Figure 1 is redrawn, and v2 adds the layer plots in Figure 4 and Tables 11–13. Existing displays are resized and relocated, including v1 Table 10 becoming main-text Table 4. The original detoxification examples remain as renumbered Figures 5–6.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves reproducibility by identifying the retain corpus and supplying SFT prompts and resource details. The layer analysis addresses the previously untested target-layer choice, and Appendix E adds meaningful applicability limits. These gains are limited by unexplained revisions to monitoring scores, the absence of repeated-run uncertainty for the added experiments, and scalability claims extending beyond the reported evidence.
